newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador Bradys plummet after reversal in rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador Bradys plummet after reversal in rate rise.

text.p: Ecuador's Brady bonds sank Thursday after President Abdala Bucaram decided to freeze fuel prices and suspend price increases for gas and electricity which have sparked social unrest.

"This is unleashing a lot of uncertainty into the market...and people are going to start dumping out of the debt," said Walter Molano, director of economic and financial research for Latin America at SBC Warburg in New York.
Ecuadorian PDIs ECPDI=RR tumbled 2-5/8 to 59-3/8 bid and its discount bonds ECDISC=RR fell 1-5/8 to 68-5/8 bid.
Sources said the country's severe social unrest and political pressures continued to scare investors away from the country's Brady bonds.

Union supporters on the second day of a 48-hour strike continued to convey their dismay with President Abdala Bucaram and the country's tough economic austerity measures. They were calling for Congress to depose Bucaram.
Fabian Alarcon, the speaker of Ecuador's Congress, called legislators to a special session on Thursday to discuss the political fate of Bucaram.
However, Alacran refused to tell reporters on Thursday whether Congress would seek to depose the president at the congressional session scheduled to start at 1700 EST/2300 GMT.
Molano said Ecuador PDIs could conceivably drop to about 58 or 57 before a possible turnaround.
He said the illiquid Ecuadorian Brady market can simply move in "a step-function" type pattern, depending on the outcome of the special Congressionial session Thursday evening.
"If Congress decides to impeach (Bucaram), he refuses to go, the military steps in...I can easily see (PDIs) opening up at around 58 tomorrow morning."
However, Molano said if the current political situation lingers for the next several days, the decline will be gradual.
